{{ill|Kisao Ozaki|ja|尾崎喜左雄|qid=Q21698487}} proposed that Takeuchi Shrine (Sukune Shrine) was originally Kawanami no Sukune Shrine. He interpreted “Kawanami” as “river” and “Sukune” as “chokune,” understanding the shrine name to mean “the main current of the river.” He explained that because three shrines—{{ill|Kawasukune Shrine (Higashiagatsuma)|ja|甲波宿禰神社 (東吾妻町)|qid=Q66085131|lt=Hakoshima}}, Obashima, and Kawashima—were lined up along the {{ill|Agatsuma River|ar|نهر أجاتسوما|arz|نهر اجاتسوما|ceb|Agatsuma Gawa|fa|رود اگاتسوما|fr|Agatsuma-gawa|it|Agatsuma (fiume)|ja|吾妻川|ru|Агацума (река)|qid=Q1636255}} in places with “shima” (island) in their names, they represented the deification of the Agatsuma River itself.<ref>{{Cite book|Japanese |title=Studies on the Jinmyōchō of Kōzuke Province |date=1974-12-10 |year=1974 |publisher=Ozaki Sensei Chosho Kankōkai |pages=210-212 |last=Ozaki |author=Kizao Ozaki |first=Kizao |author-link=Kizao Ozaki |doi=10.11501/12266236}}{{Registration required}}</ref>

An engraved inscription dated the 8th year of {{ill|Hōei|fa|هوئی (دوره)|fr|Ère Hōei|ja|宝永|ko|호에이|ru|Хоэй|simple|Hōei|sr|Хоеи|sv|Hōei|tr|Hōei|zh|寶永|qid=Q1145262}} ({{ill|1711|ab|1711|af|1711|als|1711|am|1711 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1711|ar|1711|ary|1711|arz|1711|ast|1711|avk|1711|az|1711|azb|۱۷۱۱ (میلادی)|ba|1711 йыл|ban|1711|bar|1711|bcl|1711|be|1711|be_x_old|1711|bg|1711|bn|১৭১১|bo|༡༧༡༡ལོ།|bpy|মারি ১৭১১|br|1711|bs|1711.|ca|1711|cdo|1711 nièng|ceb|1711|ckb|١٧١١|co|1711|crh|1711|cs|1711|csb|1711|cv|1711|cy|1711|da|1711|de|1711|diq|1711|el|1711|eml|1711|eo|1711|es|1711|et|1711|eu|1711|fa|۱۷۱۱ (میلادی)|fi|1711|fo|1711|fr|1711|frp|1711|frr|1711|fur|1711|fy|1711|ga|1711|gan|1711年|gcr|1711|gd|1711|gl|1711|gv|1711|he|1711|hi|१७११|hr|1711.|hsb|1711|ht|1711 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1711|hy|1711|hyw|1711 թուական|ia|1711|id|1711|ilo|1711|io|1711|is|1711|it|1711|ja|1711年|jv|1711|ka|1711|kaa|1711|kk|1711 жыл|kn|೧೭೧೧|ko|1711년|krc|1711 джыл|kv|1711 во|la|1711|lb|1711|lez|1711 йис|li|1711|lij|1711|lmo|1711|lt|1711 m.|lv|1711. gads|mai|१७११|map_bms|1711|mdf|1711|mg|1711|mhr|1711|mi|1711|min|1711|mk|1711|mr|इ.स. १७११|mrj|1711 и|ms|1711|my|၁၇၁၁|myv|1711 ие|mzn|۱۷۱۱|nap|1711|nds|1711|new|सन् १७११|nl|1711|nn|1711|no|1711|nrm|1711|nso|1711|oc|1711|olo|1711|or|୧୭୧୧|os|1711-æм аз|pa|1711|pl|1711|pnb|1711|pt|1711|qu|1711|ro|1711|ru|1711 год|rue|1711|sa|१७११|sah|1711|sc|1711|scn|1711|sd|1711ع|se|1711|sh|1711.|shn|1711|si|1711|simple|1711|sk|1711|sl|1711|smn|1711|sq|1711|sr|1711|su|1711|sv|1711|sw|1711|szl|1711|ta|1711|te|1711|tg|Соли 1711|th|พ.ศ. 2254|tk|1711|tl|1711|tr|1711|tt|1711 ел|uk|1711|ur|1711ء|uz|1711|vec|1711|vi|1711|vls|1711|vo|1711|wa|1711|war|1711|wuu|1711年|xmf|1711|yi|1711|zh|1711年|zh_classical|一七一一年|zh_min_nan|1711 nî|zh_yue|1711年|qid=Q6866}}) is found on the {{ill|Giboshi|de|Gibōshi|fr|Gibōshi|ja|擬宝珠|zh|擬寶珠|qid=Q3105399}} of the balustrade of the main hall, and thus that year is considered the year of construction{{Sfn|Shibukawa City History Compilation Committee|1993|pp=883-884}}.

The shrine buildings are located atop a high ground known as Ubazuka{{Sfn|Shibukawa City History Compilation Committee|1993|pp=883-884}}. Although it was once thought to be a {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|ko|전방후원분|simple|Zenpō-kōen-fun|zh|前方後圓墳|qid=Q11268718}}, it is in fact a natural {{ill|Hügelland|cs|Pahorkatina|de|Hügelland|fr|Basse montagne|hak|Khiu-lîn|ja|丘陵|ko|구릉|nl|Heuvelland (landschap)|pl|Wysoczyzna|sk|Pahorkatina|zh|丘陵|zh_classical|丘陵|zh_yue|丘陵|qid=Q222912}}{{Sfn|Shibukawa City History Compilation Committee|1993|p=117}}. There is a local tradition that this was the place where {{ill|Yamato Takeru|arz|ياماتو تاكيرو|be|Ямата Такэру|de|Yamatotakeru|es|Yamato Takeru|fa|یاماتو تاکه‌رو|fr|Yamato Takeru|hu|Jamatotakeru|id|Yamato Takeru|it|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル|ko|야마토타케루|pt|Yamato Takeru|ru|Ямато Такэру|sh|Yamato Takeru|simple|Yamato Takeru|sq|Jamato Takeru|sr|Јамато Такеру|sv|Yamato Takeru|tr|Yamato Takeru|uk|Ямато Такеру|ur|یاماتو تاکیرو|vi|Yamato Takeru|zh|日本武尊|zh_min_nan|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru}}’s wife {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Uwagitsuhime}} and their child lived, and that Ubazuka is the grave of Uwagitsuhime, which is said to be the origin of the place name Obashima{{Sfn|Shibukawa City History Compilation Committee|1984|p=903}}.

==Festivals==
* April 3 – Spring annual festival{{Sfn|Shibukawa City History Compilation Committee|1986|p=542}}
* July 25 – Gion Festival; a festival of the enshrined Yasaka Shrine, during which a portable shrine is paraded{{Sfn|Shibukawa City History Compilation Committee|1986|p=542}}.
* October 9 – Autumn annual festival{{Sfn|Shibukawa City History Compilation Committee|1986|p=542}}
